input.quote: (a) Assignment. Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class.
input.rationale: The assignment architecture is symmetric and preserves our successor rights, so it sits at or above the fallback. Section 10.2(a) is expressly subject to Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6: Section 5.3 lets our Depositor pass this Agreement to any Person into which it merges or consolidates, that succeeds to its business, or that is an Affiliate to whom it assigns, without counterparty consent — the affiliate/successor and M&A carve-out the preferred position requires (the 15-Business-Day assumption agreement, Officer's Certificate/Opinion and Rating Agency notice are mechanical successor formalities, close to the fallback's "written notice"). Section 7.6 gives Cellco as Servicer the mirror-image right, and the residual consent gate in 10.2(a) runs to the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and Noteholders (investor protection) rather than to Cellco, so the counterparty holds no veto over our assignments. The Issuer's ability to assign and pledge to the Indenture Trustee is expressly acknowledged (Section 2.2), and Section 10.2(b) binds permitted successors and assigns. On change of control: the phrase appears nowhere in the Agreement, and there is no Cellco right to terminate, re-price or refuse consent on a change of control of the Issuer or Depositor — to the contrary, Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer unless it is legally unable to perform. The Class A Certificateholder's Optional Acquisition/Optional Redemption rights (Sections 8.1–8.2) are principal-balance and date triggered, not change-of-control triggered, so they are not a walk-away exit right. Noted but not flagged: consent under 10.2(a) is not qualified by a "not unreasonably withheld" standard and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor, both minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording in a structured-finance deal where the consent parties are the trustees and noteholders.
